title: Hidden Frustration in Collinear Altermagnets: Pairing Vortices and Equilibrium Spin Current Loops
abstract: We show that a magnet can remain perfectly collinear while its quantum vacuum circulates. In a centrosymmetric altermagnet, a symmetry-allowed locally staggered Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling imprints a gauge-irremovable vortex-antivortex pair into the anomalous magnon pair correlations at high-symmetry points in momentum space. In real space, these hidden vortices produce an antiferrochiral array of equilibrium spin currents circulating oppositely around neighboring plaquettes. Gauge-irremovable frustration therefore survives despite classical collinearity: it exists entirely in the quantum correlations. Our results show that complex pairing, gauge-invariant fluxes, and equilibrium loop currents - structures encountered across electronic flux phases, spin liquids, and frustrated quantum magnets - can be encoded in the squeezed vacuum of a collinear magnet.
summary: This work demonstrates that even when a magnet maintains a simple, collinear classical spin structure, quantum correlations can harbor hidden frustration. This frustration is induced by a symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, leading to topological vortices in the magnon correlations. These vortices manifest macroscopically as a pattern of counter-circulating, equilibrium spin currents in the quantum vacuum.
main_problem: The paper investigates how hidden frustration, manifested as circulating quantum correlations, can exist in a magnet that remains classically collinear.
main_result: The system hosts a frustrated, current-carrying quantum vacuum despite classical collinearity, driven by symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling.
method: The analysis uses Holstein-Primakoff expansion, Bogoliubov diagonalization for magnon modes, and topological diagnostics like Berry curvature and Wilson loops.
model_or_system: The study focuses on a 2D inverse Lieb lattice realized in a centrosymmetric altermagnet insulator, modeled by a spin Hamiltonian including exchange and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
key_observables: Anomalous magnon pair correlations, gauge-invariant fluxes, and antiferrochiral equilibrium spin currents.
important_parameters:
The regime requires $J_1 > 0$, $D_1

main_assumptions: The analysis is performed using linear spin-wave theory (Holstein-Primakoff expansion) and assumes a centrosymmetric structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model lattice, the phase accumulation of the anomalous correlator $F_k$ showing vortices at high-symmetry points (X and Y), and vector plots of the Berry connection and curvature showing opposite-chirality vortices.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the Hamiltonian, linearizing it via Holstein-Primakoff, calculating magnon dispersions, identifying topological features (vortices) in the anomalous correlators, and finally deriving the real-space consequences as counter-circulating spin currents.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent, non-trivial quantum fluxes and currents existing entirely within the quantum vacuum, decoupled from static magnetic order, is highly relevant to understanding topological phases in condensed matter systems.
